summary: Carefully documented preregistered paired experiment that implemented a deterministic validator + single-iteration repair pipeline for LLM→NetOps configuration generation. Execution artifacts and hashes are extensive and the manuscript transparently reports that baseline single-shot generation was near‑ceiling (299/300) so the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction hypothesis was not supported. Methods, preregistration fidelity, and archival provenance are strong; the main shortcomings are manuscript presentation (metadata-heavy, reads partly as an artifact report) and a few clarifications needed to fully satisfy conference-style scholarly norms.
critical_issues: Manuscript currently reads in part as an artifact/audit report rather than focused conference prose: excessive run-internal paths, hashes, and provenance details appear in the main narrative instead of being referenced concisely and delegated to the archived evidence bundle.

The paper lacks an explicit, succinct statement in Methods/Results that the preregistered sensitivity treatment(s) for failed model calls (the 'failure-as-zero' sensitivity) were executed and produced identical conclusions; the text implies this but does not report the sensitivity numeric result explicitly.

The presentation includes many low‑level execution artifacts and file paths in the main manuscript (e.g., explicit raw results paths and some full hashes). Per the track guidelines these should be summarized and the full artifact manifest referenced, not quoted verbatim in body text.
required_revisions: Condense provenance/metadata in the main manuscript: remove or substantially shorten inline file paths and full hashes, relocate detailed artifact-hash manifest and raw-path listings to the archived evidence bundle and cite them succinctly (e.g., ‘artifact bundle, execution_manifest.json’). Ensure the Disclosure Statement remains complete but concise on pages 1–5.

Explicitly report the preregistered sensitivity analysis numeric outcome(s) in Methods or Results (the planned 'failure_as_zero' sensitivity and any other preregistered treatments). If the sensitivity yields identical counts/metrics, state that explicitly and cite the archived artifact that verifies this.

Revise the narrative to reduce artifact-inventory tone and strengthen literature-grounded scholarly prose: emphasize prior work, methodological rationale, interpretation, and limitations rather than enumerating execution files. Reformat any remaining provenance mentions into a short paragraph pointing readers to the archived manifest (included as evidence).
optional_revisions: Add a brief per-category failure table or summary (reachability/ACL/routing/syntax) even if counts are zero — this improves clarity for readers and aligns with preregistered secondary estimands (can be populated from archived scoring artifacts).

Include a one‑paragraph recommendation for future preregistrations describing how to choose generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent draws) to preserve statistical power for McNemar-style paired tests.

Where space permits, add a short paragraph contrasting the deterministic validator’s coverage vs. full dynamic emulation and indicate which concrete validator rules were exercised most frequently (can be drawn from archived validator traces).
